literature.title: Management of splenic abscess in children by percutaneous drainage.

literature.title: Quinolone-resistant Salmonella paratyphi B meningitis in a newborn: a case report.

瀰漫性系統性硬皮症（dcSSc）為自體免疫性纖維化疾病，病理機轉涉及 TGF-β 纖維化路徑、血管內皮功能障礙及免疫失調。Amikacin 為純抗菌機轉，與 dcSSc 的免疫病理無合理連結。TxGNN 高分可能源於知識圖譜中「藥物-蛋白質-疾病」的間接路徑（如共享蛋白質節點），非真實治療相關性的反映。

literature.title: Malaria and typhoid fever among patients presenting with febrile illnesses in Ga West Municipality, Ghana.
literature.abstract: Clinicians in areas where malaria and typhoid fever are co-endemic often treat infected patients irrationally, which may lead to the emergence of drug resistance and extra cost to patients. literature.title: Infarction of spleen in typhoid fever.
literature.abstract: Ultrasonography and computed tomography scan with hypo echoic areas diagnosed a splenic infarction in a Salmonella typhi infected 30-year-old man with painful hypochondrium and epigastrium. Imaging techniques contribute remarkably to a rapid diagnosis and rational management of the extra intestinal lesions attributable to the Salmonella typhi/paratyphi group of organisms.

literature.title: Salmonella typhi endocarditis: a case report.
literature.abstract: Salmonella are a rare cause of infective endocarditis. This report describes a case where Salmonella typhi was isolated from the blood and urine of a patient with echocardiographically documented aortic valve disease and endocarditis. The patient was treated with two weeks of ceftriaxone (3 g/day) and amikacin (15 mg/kg/day), followed by a further two weeks of ceftriaxone (3 g/day) alone. He made a complete recovery.

literature.title: Recent advances in management of bacterial meningitis in neonates.
literature.abstract: The current incidence of neonatal sepsis in the United States varies from less than 1 to 8.1 per 1000 live births. The incidence of bacterial meningitis is about one-third of the number of infants with sepsis. The mortality is 20 to 30% and many survivors are severely impaired. Group B streptococcus and Escherichia coli are the most frequent causes of meningitis. literature.title: [Neonatal meningitis due to Enterococcus spp.: presentation of four cases].
literature.abstract: Enterococci are unusual etiologic agents of bacterial meningitis and account for only 0.3-4% of all cases. Neonatal enterococcal meningitis, which is rarely reported in the medical literature, presents characteristics that are significantly different from enterococcal meningitis affecting other age groups, particularly adults.
